The detaining authority relied on the aforesaid three (03) crimes for passing the detention order, but the allegations levelled against the detenus in the said crimes affect the specific individual and not the public at large.
i) She would further submit that the detention orders were passed without application of mind and subjective satisfaction.

Preventive detention of a person is an extreme measure resorted to by KL,J &
PSS,J W.P. Nos.14064 & 13620 of 2023 the State when ordinary criminal law is found not adequate to control his activities which cause disturbance to public order.
In the cases on hand, there is no disturbance caused to public order and the alleged offences are between the individuals.
5. She would further submit that respondent No.2 detaining authority did not follow the procedure laid down under the Act No.1 of 1986.

that sufficiency of grounds is not for the Court but for the detaining authority for the formation of subjective act in any manner prejudicial to public order is required and that such satisfaction is subjective and not objective.

The object of the law of preventive detention is not punitive, but only preventive and further that the action of the executive in detaining a person being only precautionary, normally, the matter has necessarily to be left to the discretion of the executive authority.
It is not practicable to lay down objective rules of conduct in an exhaustive manner.
The satisfaction of the detaining authority, therefore, is considered to be of primary importance with certain latitude in the exercise of its discretion.

21. As discussed supra, in the present case, the detaining authority considered the nature of offence and the manner in which the detenus have committed the same and also the modes operandi adopted of the detenus in committing the offence.

Therefore, on coming to the subjective satisfaction, the detaining authority has issued the aforesaid detention orders both dated 01.05.2023 against KL,J & PSS,J W.P. Nos.14064 & 13620 of 2023 both the detenus as preventive measures to prevent them in committing the similar offence.

22. In Pushkar Mukherjee4, the Apex Court held that the difference between the concepts of a "public order" and "law and order" is similar to the distinction between "public" and "private"
crimes in the realms of jurisprudence.

In considering the material elements of crime, the historic tests which each community applies are "intrinsic wrongfulness" and social expediency which are the two most important factors which have led to the designation of certain conduct as criminal.

Supreme Court also discussed that Dr. Allen who has distinguished "public" and "private" crimes in the sense that some offences primarily injure specific persons and only secondarily the public interest, while others directly injure the public interest and affect individuals only remotely.
There is a broad distinction along these lines, but differences naturally arise in the application of any such test.

It was further held that the order of detention would be invalid even if there were other relevant grounds because it can never be certain to what extent the bad reasons operated on the mind of the authority concerned or whether the detention order would have been made at all if only one or two good reasons had been before them.
As discussed supra, the detaining authority considering the entire material on record issued detention orders against both the detenus to prevent them for committing the similar offences.

One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of state.
It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State.

sentences.text: What this Court stated in Ramesh Yadav was that ordinarily a detention order should not be passed merely to pre-empt or circumvent enlargement on bail in cases which are essentially criminal in nature and can be dealt with under the ordinary law.
It seems to us well settled that even in a case where a person is in custody, if the facts and circumstances of the case so demand, resort can be had to the law of preventive detention.
This seems to be quite clear from the case law discussed above and there is no need to refer to the High Court decisions to which our attention was drawn since they do not hold otherwise.

We, therefore, find it difficult to accept the contention of the counsel for the petitioners that there was no valid and compelling reason for passing the impugned orders of detention because the detenus were in custody."

32. In view of the same, the contention of the petitioner that the detaining authority has violated the procedure laid down under Act No.1 of 1986 cannot be accepted.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that the detaining authority have relied on three cases while issuing impugned detention order and out of which only one case is within territorial jurisdiction of respondent No.2 - detaining authority and other two cases are not within his jurisdiction and without considering the said facts, detaining authority has issued detention orders both dated 01.05.2023 contrary to Section 3(2) of the Act No.1 of 1986.
34.

As per Section 3(2) of the Act No.1 of 1986, the detaining authority shall consider the circumstances prevailing or likely to prevail in any area within the local limits of the jurisdiction of a District Magistrate or a Commissioner of Police, the Government are satisfied that it is necessary so to do, they may, by order in writing, direct that during such period as may be specified in the order,
such District Magistrate or Commissioner of Police may also, if satisfied as provided in sub-section (1), exercise the powers conferred by the said sub-section.
35 . It is also not in dispute that order of detention can be passed basing on solitary offence.
However, the detaining authority shall consider the nature of offence and manner in which it was committed.
KL,J & PSS,J W.P. Nos.14064 & 13620 of 2023
In the present case, the detaining authority relied on one case committed by the detenus within its jurisdiction and the remaining two cases were not committed within its jurisdiction.

However, considering the entire material on record and also nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed, modes operandi and on coming to subjective satisfaction only, the detaining authority has passed the impugned detention order.
36. As discussed supra, in Arun Ghosh2, the Apex Court held that public order was said to embrace more of the community than law and order.
Public order is even tempo of the life of the community taking the country as a whole or even a specified locality.
Disturbance of public order is to be distinguished, from acts directed against individuals which do not disturb the society to the extent of causing a general disturbance of public tranquility.
It is the degree of disturbance and its effect upon the life of the community in a locality which determines whether the disturbance amounts only to a breach of law and order.
37. In the light of the aforesaid discussion, the contention of learned counsel for the petitioners cannot be accepted.

sentences.text: The Apex Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration17 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.
The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.
39. As discussed above, the detaining authority on consideration of entire material and on coming to subjective satisfaction issued the impugned detention order and confirmed the same.
There is no irregularity.

40. Therefore, according to us, there is no violation of Section 3(2) of the Act No.1 of 1986 by the respondent No.2 - detaining authority while issuing detention orders both dated 01.05.2023.
41.

In the light of the aforesaid discussion, we are of the considered view that there is no error and violation of the procedure committed by respondent No.2 - detaining Authority while issuing impugned detention orders both dated 01.05.2023 and confirmation orders of respondent No.1.
Both the Writ Petitions are liable to be . (1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & PSS,J W.P. Nos.14064 & 13620 of 2023 dismissed and accordingly the same are dismissed.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petitions shall stand closed.

Upon considering the said aspects, Apex Court held that if there are compelling reasons to justify his preventive detention orders against the detenus, the Detaining Authority shall consider the entire material on record and shall come to subjective satisfaction that the detenus must be prevented from committing similar offences.
Public Order is the even tempo of the life of the community taking the country as a whole or even a specified locality. .

Disturbance of Public Order is to be distinguished from acts directed against individuals which do not disturb the society to the extent of causing a general disturbance of public tranquility.
It is the degree of disturbance and its affect upon the life of the community in a locality which determines whether the disturbance amounts only to a breach of law and order.
Thus,
Apex Court held that the Detaining Authority shall consider the entire material on record and come to a subjective satisfaction that the acts of the detenu have caused disturbance to the public at large.

It was further held that the order of detention would be invalid even if there were other relevant grounds because it can never be certain to what extent the bad reasons operated on the mind of the authority concerned or whether the detention order would have been made at all if only one or two good reasons had been before them.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that the detaining authority have relied on three cases while issuing impugned detention order and out of which only one case is within territorial jurisdiction of respondent No.2 - detaining authority and other two cases are not within his jurisdiction and without considering the said facts, detaining authority has issued detention orders both dated 01.05.2023 contrary to Section 3(2) of the Act No.1 of 1986.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On consideration of the entire material available on record and also the nature of offence and the manner in which the offence was committed, on coming to the subjective satisfaction, respondent No.2/Detaining Authority has passed the impugned detention order against both the detenus.
The respondent No.1 confirmed the said orders basing on the report of advisory board.
There is no error in the detention orders and confirmation orders.
The object of the law of preventive detention is not punitive, but only preventive and further that the action of the executive in detaining a person being only precautionary, normally, the matter has necessarily to be left to the discretion of the executive authority.
It is not practicable to lay down objective rules of conduct in an exhaustive manner.
The satisfaction of the detaining authority, therefore, is considered to be of primary importance with certain latitude in the exercise of its discretion.
Therefore, on coming to the subjective satisfaction, the detaining authority has issued the aforesaid detention orders both dated 01.05.2023 against KL,J & PSS,J W.P. Nos.14064 & 13620 of 2023 both the detenus as preventive measures to prevent them in committing the similar offence.

13620 of 2023 therein did not apply its mind and without coming to the subjective satisfaction issued detention order against the detenu therein and therefore held that that detention order is illegal.
In the present case, the Detaining Authority considered the nature of offence and the manner in which the offence was committed and issued impugned detention order against both the detenus.
In the present case, the detaining authority relied on one case committed by the detenus within its jurisdiction and the remaining two cases were not committed within its jurisdiction.
However, considering the entire material on record and also nature of offence and the manner in which it was committed, modes operandi and on coming to subjective satisfaction only, the detaining authority has passed the impugned detention order.
Disturbance of public order is to be distinguished, from acts directed against individuals which do not disturb the society to the extent of causing a general disturbance of public tranquility.
It is the degree of disturbance and its effect upon the life of the community in a locality which determines whether the disturbance amounts only to a breach of law and order.
The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.
There is no irregularity.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the light of the aforesaid discussion, we are of the considered view that there is no error and violation of the procedure committed by respondent No.2 - detaining Authority while issuing impugned detention orders both dated 01.05.2023 and confirmation orders of respondent No.1.
Both the Writ Petitions are liable to be . (1982) 2 SCC 403 KL,J & PSS,J W.P. Nos.14064 & 13620 of 2023 dismissed and accordingly the same are dismissed.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petitions shall stand closed.
